newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Chartists say Swedish crown set to weaken vs mark.
newsitem.headline: Chartists say Swedish crown set to weaken vs mark.

text.p: The Swedish crown, which has been moving in a wedge formation since a strong point around 4.30 to the mark last October, is expected to break out soon and embark on further weakening, several technical analysts say.

Anders Soderberg, a technical analyst at Credit Agricole Indosuez, said he had raised his level of major resistance to 4.5200 from 4.5050 on Monday and that piercing this would mean the crown was set to move along a fresh upward chart path.
"In that case we can say with confidence we have now got the (chart) low for this time and can focus on the upside," he told Reuters.
Because the crown is quoted in terms of the number needed to buy a mark, the chart is effectively upside down, a chart rise indicating a weaking currency and vice-versa.
The ideal target would be 4.72 to 4.74 if it broke through, Soderberg said.
The 4.50 level was extremely important in the long-term in part because of speculation about Sweden linking its currency to ERM2 and a possible psychological barrier, Soderberg said.
"There's always a lot of guessing about when and where Sweden will find a midpoint to join a possible ERM2...but people believe it should be a sort of maximum 4.50," Soderberg said.
"Whether it goes up or down it seems to find its way back to the area around 4.50. " he said.
Patric Naeslund, technical analyst at Swedbank, said the currency was in a wedge formation with 4.56 as the upper limit and 4.47 at the bottom with resistance at 4.50 and 4.5150.
"In the medium term perspective we're still very easily in the wedge but within the wedge I expect some movement on the upside," Naeslund told Reuters.
However, he said this upward movement would be limited because the mark/lira cross broke downside and this would probably weigh heavily on the mark/stocky, or Swedish crown.

HSBC Midland economist Peter Lindquist said the crown would probably stay in the range of a support level at 4.4650 and resistance at 4.4950. He said it was unlikely to break at 4.4650 but if it does it would test 4.45 soon.
The crown should strengthen in the medium term, however.

"It's quite an interesting triangle pattern at the moment. It's been ranging in that pattern for quite sometime. If it does break 4.4650 it's going to move quite aggressively -- to 4.42 or 4.40 even," Lindquist said.
But Nordbanken technical analyst Bijan Fahimi said the long-term view was particularly difficult to call.
"Since October we have seen higher and higher bottoms and since March lower and lower highs," Fahimi told Reuters.
"I am neutral to slightly bullish for the crown in the short-term but in the long-term from a technical point-of-view the trend is very unclear," he said.
